prediction_question: For an item-premise pair in Malaysia's official daily price-monitoring panel that was actively quoted in week W (at least 3 observations that week), will the pair's weekly modal price be HIGHER in week W+1 than in week W? The panel is the KPDN/DOSM PriceCatcher programme (2,158 premises, 343 items measured in the 2026-08/09 sample), so this is a week-ahead retail price-increase prediction at item x premise grain.
prediction_time: End of week W (Sunday 23:59:59 MYT = UTC+8, i.e. 15:59:59 UTC). Features may use only price observations with date <= end of week W, from files whose data_as_of is within week W or earlier. The publisher's storage channel is measured to carry rows dated the same day (2026-10-21 rows present in the 2026-10 file, file last-modified 2026-10-21 12:10 UTC), so no publication lag is incurred for the feature instant; the label (week W+1 modal price) is computable from files available by day 2 of week W+2 at the latest (current-month file refreshes daily; a completed month's file was last modified 12 days after month end, 2026-09 file -> 2026-10-12, so construction snapshots and hashes monthly files at freeze time - see construction notes).
target_definition: Binary: modal(price of item i at premise p over all observations in ISO week W+1) > modal(same over week W). Modal price = most frequent observed price that week (ties broken by higher price, deterministic). Pairs with <3 observations in either week are excluded from that transition's rows (exclusion is a function of data through week W+1, applied identically everywhere; it affects ~3% of subsample pairs). The label source columns are the W+1 price observations themselves: no price observation with date > end of week W may ship as a feature column; the shipped target is 0/1.

sources.name: PriceCatcher: Transactional Records - Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) and Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), published through the national open-data portal data.gov.my / OpenDOSM
sources.url: https://data.gov.my/data-catalogue/pricecatcher (dataset page with variable definitions and licence); bulk files at https://storage.data.gov.my/pricecatcher/pricecatcher_YYYY-MM.csv and .parquet
sources.api: Anonymous bulk HTTP(S) download of one CSV/parquet per calendar month, 58 editions measured (2022-01 through 2026-10 inclusive). No API for this dataset by design: the publisher states on the dataset page 'This data catalog is not available through OpenAPI as the nature of the data makes it unsuitable for API access'; the generic catalogue API (https://api.data.gov.my/data-catalogue/?id=pricecatcher) answers 404, measured.
sources.license: Per-dataset licence statement measured on the dataset page (fetched 2026-10-21): 'This data is made open under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0). A copy of the license is available Here' with link to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/.
sources.access: No key, no registration, no rate wall measured. Two 45-50 MB month files downloaded in 3.7-3.8 s each from the coordinator. Current-month file is refreshed same-day (2026-10 file last-modified 2026-10-21 12:10 UTC and carries rows dated 2026-10-21).

sources.name: PriceCatcher lookup tables: Premise Lookup and Item Lookup (same publisher and licence)
sources.access: premise_code -> premise, address, premise_type, state, district; item_code -> item, unit, item_group, item_category. 797 items in the lookup across 60 categories (measured).

license_evidence: Measured 2026-10-21 from https://data.gov.my/data-catalogue/pricecatcher (HTML, page-embedded metadata license_text): 'This data is made open under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0). A copy of the license is available Here'. The same statement is served by OpenDOSM's mirror (open.dosm.gov.my/data-catalogue/pricecatcher, retrieved via search 2026-10-21).

CC BY 4.0 permits redistribution and commercial use with attribution; the attribution requirement carries through unchanged to any release. No share-alike, no NC restriction. No risk acceptance needed.

Publisher caveat measured on the dataset page: the data is collected for price surveillance, is 'excellent for high-frequency analysis of specific items in specific locations', and 'Inflation analysis should be conducted using DOSM's CPI data' - the task below is a pair-level micro-pricing task, not inflation nowcasting, consistent with the publisher's own stated scope.
split_strategy: Temporal splits on ISO-week transitions, disjoint and ordered: candidate windows (to be fixed at construction from the full 58-month archive, ~250 weekly transitions 2022-01..2026-10): train on transitions up to 2024-12, eval on 2025 transitions, holdout on 2026 transitions (exact windows fixed at construction). Each weekly transition carries both classes: measured increase rate 15.5%-22.2% and decrease rate 14.5%-20.1% across all 7 measured transitions (Aug-Sep 2026, 10% premise subsample), so class balance holds window-to-window. Positives cluster by item: 54-58 distinct items show >=1 increasing pair per transition, and the top-10 items carry 38-45% of positive pairs - the clustered event count (item-level, not pair-level) must be reported per split and is ~55/week in the subsample (~170/week full panel, estimate). Cross-split identifier policy: item-premise pairs (and premises/items) recur across windows by design - the panel is longitudinal - so entity keys are NOT split-exclusive; the no-cross-split-entities check does not apply to pair panels where the same pair legitimately appears in many weekly transitions. This must be declared in quality.json (expected_duplicate_ids / documented repeats) at construction, mirroring the runner-contract handling of longitudinal panels.

measurements.access_probes_2026_10_21: https://data.gov.my/ HTTP 200 (142,373 B); https://developer.data.gov.my/ HTTP 200 (48,218 B, documents Data Catalogue API, OpenDOSM API, Transport/GTFS, Weather APIs); https://api.data.gov.my/data-catalogue/?id=pricecatcher&limit=6 HTTP 404 'The data catalogue (pricecatcher) requested does not exist' (measured - bulk-only for this dataset); https://storage.data.gov.my/pricecatcher/pricecatcher_2026-09.csv HEAD 200 content-length 45,137,790 last-modified 2026-10-12 06:42:57 GMT; pricecatcher_2026-10.csv HEAD 200 content-length 20,407,078 last-modified 2026-10-21 12:10:13 GMT (current month, still filling); pricecatcher_2022-01.csv HEAD 200 content-length 65,359,198; pricecatcher_2026-09-01.csv HEAD 404 (filename pattern is YYYY-MM, not YYYY-MM-DD).
measurements.panel_shape_2026_10_21: Measured on full 2026-08 (1,933,285 rows, 29 of 31 days, 2026-08-01..2026-08-30) and 2026-09 (1,742,320 rows, 28 of 30 days, 2026-09-01..2026-09-29) files: 2,158 distinct premises x 343 distinct items; 0 duplicate (date, premise_code, item_code) rows; schema date,premise_code,item_code,price; mean row length 25.9 B. Publisher states 'over a million price records per month' and 'collected and verified by groundstaff on a daily basis' (dataset page); a parliamentary written reply reported by The Star (2025-12-04) corroborates the panel: '2,170 premises and keeps tabs on 316 items across six categories, supported by more than 850 price monitoring officers'. Monthly files can have missing collection days (29/31 and 28/30 measured), which the >=3 observations/week threshold absorbs.
measurements.label_structure_2026_10_21: Weekly modal-price transitions measured on a 10% premise subsample (premise_code % 10 == 0; 216 premises, 326 items, 179,707 pair-weeks from 375,665 rows), 7 transitions with both weeks >=6 covered days: increase rate 0.2217/0.1947/0.1823/0.1774/0.1809/0.1548/0.1875, decrease rate 0.1604/0.1950/0.2014/0.1621/0.1791/0.1862/0.1448, flat rate 0.61-0.67; 3,911-4,031 eligible pairs per transition in the subsample (~40,000 full panel, estimate). Both classes present in every transition. Persistence rule for this task: predicting 'no increase' scores 78-84% accuracy - the AUC-relevant base rate (~18%) is far from degenerate, and the task is a change forecast, not a level forecast, so the persistence baseline is beatable in principle; the triad (persistence, calendar-only, model) must be measured at construction before any number is quoted.
measurements.clustering_2026_10_21: Positives cluster by item: 54-58 distinct items with >=1 increasing pair per transition; top-10 items carry 38-45% of positive pairs. The per-transition clustered event count (~55 items in subsample) and its interval go into the record at construction.
measurements.extraction_cost_2026_10_21: Measured from the coordinator: each month CSV is 45,137,790-65,359,198 B (measured for 2026-09 and 2022-01; 2026-08 measured at 50,122,871 B) and downloads in ~3.7-3.8 s (~12-13 MB/s). Full 58-edition window is therefore ~2.6-3.5 GB and ~58 HTTP requests (estimate derived from 3 measured file sizes; labelled estimate). Worker-side full extraction is trivially within budget; the coordinator probe was capped at 2 month files (95 MB, deleted after measurement, never committed).
measurements.publication_schedule_2026_10_21: Current-month file refreshed same-day (2026-10-21 rows present at 12:10 UTC refresh); a completed month's file last-modified 12 days after month end (2026-09 -> 2026-10-12). The portal's own data-request ticket log (https://data.gov.my/data-request, retrieved via search 2026-10-21) records a 2026-10-06 rejected ticket complaining the pricecatcher table had not updated in >1 week (data as of 24 Sep) - updates can stall for a week+, so construction must snapshot and hash the monthly files it uses and record their last-modified dates as the observed lag evidence in quality.json's timing block.
measurements.known_event_fixtures_for_construction: External, dated policy events to land as fixtures when the full archive is built: (1) diesel subsidy rationalisation of 2024-06-10 (pump diesel price rose from RM2.15 to RM3.30), which should show pass-through into transport-sensitive item prices in the weeks after; (2) Malaysia's retail sugar price step-changes after sugar subsidy removal (2022-11, refined white sugar items in the lookup: GULA PUTIH BERTAPIS KASAR/HALUS, item codes 1589/1590); (3) festive-season price-control schemes (Program Subsidi Harga chicken/egg ceilings with published scheme dates). Each fixture: named event, expected direction of the item's modal price around the date, publisher source for the event date. These are construction-time checks, not measured this session.
measurements.cross_check_plan: Cross-check the built artifact against the publisher's own summary product at construction: item-level national modal prices from PriceCatcher vs the item's price series on KPDN's MyHarga/PriceCatcher consumer dashboard, and vs DOSM's published monthly average price tables, for a fixed item list.

next_action: GO to construction (advancement session owns it; this was a discovery-only session). Construction steps: (1) enumerate all 58 monthly editions and snapshot+hash the files used (record last-modified dates as observed publication-lag evidence); (2) build the pair-week panel with >=3 observations/week eligibility, modal price with deterministic tie-break; (3) construct features from data through end of week W only (pair history: weeks-since-last-change, last change size; item-level distribution signals within W: national modal, dispersion, share of premises increasing in W; premise/item/category/state metadata; calendar incl. festive windows); (4) fix split windows on the ~250 transitions (train<=2024, eval 2025, holdout 2026), declare the longitudinal-panel identifier policy and expected duplicate counts in quality.json; (5) land the known-event fixtures (diesel 2024-06-10, sugar 2022-11, festive control schemes) and the publisher cross-check; (6) run the qualification gate on the worker over the full artifact, and measure the baseline triad (persistence 'no increase', calendar-only, full model) on identical rows before any number is quoted. The 2-month coordinator probe sample (pc_2026-08.csv, pc_2026-09.csv, 95 MB) and probe scripts live uncommitted under .factory/probe/ and must be deleted, not committed.

novelty_check.theirs: KPDN/DOSM publish the raw PriceCatcher observations and lookups themselves (CC BY 4.0), a consumer app, and aggregate CPI; M5/Kaggle Store Item Demand/Rossmann/Favorita are demand-forecasting benchmarks where price is a feature and sales is the target; the price-direction classification literature is equity price movement, not retail micro-prices; no published task, splits or scored contract exists on retail week-ahead price increases at item-premise grain
novelty_check.ours: week-ahead item x premise weekly modal-price INCREASE prediction over Malaysia's official daily price-monitoring panel (2,158 premises x 343 items, 58 monthly editions 2022-01..2026-10), with leak-free feature gating (only observations through end of week W), temporal week-transition splits, measured 15-22% increase base rate, item-clustered event accounting, and dated policy-event fixtures (diesel subsidy rationalisation 2024-06-10, sugar subsidy removal 2022-11, festive price-control schemes)
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
